newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Foreign investment funds raise stakes in Colombia.
newsitem.headline: Foreign investment funds raise stakes in Colombia.

text.p: The 196 foreign investment funds authorized to operate in Colombia held nearly $1.2 billion in Colombian stocks as of last month and an additional $196 million in fixed income securities, the Securities Superintendency said Thursday.
It said the figures marked a 3.3 percent and 37 percent increase, respectively, over March. Investment in equities was up 31.86 percent over April 1996, meanwhile.
ING Barings said earlier this month that it remains overweight in Colombia, a country where it sees the strong stock market performance so far this year extending into 1998.
"Colombia remains the region's cheapest market," it said, adding that estimated 1997 and 1998 price/earnings ratios were at 11.1 times and 9.8 times, respectively.
